meta.topic: Remote Repositories & Connecting Local to GitHub

questions.question: What is a 'remote' in Git?

options.A: A physical TV remote for your monitor
options.B: A version of your repository hosted on the internet or network (e.g., on GitHub)
options.C: A developer who works from home

questions.explanation: A remote is a version of your repository hosted elsewhere, allowing you to fetch and push code to sync with others.

questions.question: What is the standard, conventional nickname given to the primary remote repository in Git?
questions.explanation: `origin` is the default shorthand name Git assigns to the remote server you cloned from or push to.

questions.question: Which command links a local repository to a remote repository URL?
questions.explanation: `git remote add <name> <url>` associates a human-readable remote name (like `origin`) with a repository web address.

questions.question: Which command lists all configured remotes along with their fetch and push URLs?
questions.explanation: `git remote -v` (verbose) lists the shortnames and exact URLs for all configured remote connections.

questions.question: When creating a GitHub repo to connect an EXISTING local project, why should you leave 'Add README' unchecked?

options.A: Because GitHub charges extra for READMEs
options.B: To avoid creating divergent initial commits on GitHub that would conflict with your local commits
options.C: Because Git cannot support README files
options.D: GitHub will delete your local files if checked

questions.explanation: Creating a README on GitHub generates a commit on the remote. If your local repo already has commits, pushing will be rejected until merged.

questions.question: Which two main protocols can you use to connect to a GitHub remote?
questions.explanation: HTTPS (using Personal Access Tokens or browser login) and SSH (using public/private SSH key pairs) are the two supported protocols.

questions.question: How do you change the URL of an existing remote called `origin`?
questions.explanation: `git remote set-url origin <new-url>` updates the target URL for the existing remote alias.

questions.question: Can a Git repository have more than one remote configured?

options.A: No, Git only permits a single remote named origin
options.B: Yes, you can configure multiple remotes (e.g., origin, upstream, staging)
options.C: Only if using GitLab, not GitHub

questions.explanation: Git supports arbitrary numbers of remotes. In open-source workflows, having `origin` (your fork) and `upstream` (original repo) is standard.

questions.question: Which command completely removes a remote named `origin` from your local repo configuration?
questions.explanation: `git remote remove origin` (or `git remote rm origin`) disconnects the remote link without deleting your local files or commits.

questions.question: Does running `git remote add origin <url>` upload your files to GitHub immediately?

options.A: Yes, it automatically uploads all commits
options.B: No, it only sets up the link bookmark; you must run `git push` to upload code
options.C: Yes, but only the README file

questions.explanation: Adding a remote is strictly configuration. No data is transferred to or from GitHub until you explicitly push or fetch.
